hook: The title borrows from a nursery rhyme, and a playground song that local children sing about the entity sits right in the middle of the file. This is a quiet, creeping horror piece set in a small English village, built around a rule about being alone indoors after dark. It contains disturbing descriptions of bodily harm, but most of the dread comes from what the cameras fail to show.
whyItMatters: The page credits S D Locke, and it is a clear example of the uncontained Keter story, where the Foundation can only watch, record and clean up afterwards. Its central idea, crookedness spreading from a house to the person inside it, turns a folk rhyme into a consistent physical rule. The file also reaches beyond itself, ending with a list of separate field logs that carry the investigation further.
thingsToNotice: The video log is the core: a timestamped, room-by-room record in which the entity appears only as distortion moving from one feed to the next. Notice how the observers keep radio silence while the test subject calls out for help, which says as much about the Foundation as about the anomaly. The playground song rewards a second look once you know the rules, since each crooked line echoes something in the description. The later update widens the scope from one house to the whole village, where the residents' silence becomes part of the mystery.
